articles.title: Kentucky State's Aminata Seck freed while another college basketball player lands in ICE custody
articles.summary: (AP) — A Kentucky State University women's basketball player from Senegal, who was arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement, has been released after s...
articles.body:
LOUISVILLE, Ky. (AP) — A Kentucky State University women's basketball player from Senegal, who was arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement , has been released after spending two months in custody.

At a hearing on Tuesday, a judge granted a $2,500 bond for Aminata Seck and it was posted Wednesday after ICE did not appeal, according to Hishem Alsalman, managing attorney of Alsalman Law Office.

Meanwhile, a men's basketball player from Mississippi Valley State has been placed in ICE custody. Qingfang Pang, who is from China, was detained on Sept. 29 and is being held at the Richwood Correctional Facility in Richwood, Louisiana, according to the ICE database.

"Mississippi Valley State University is aware of the situation involving one of our students and is deeply concerned for the student's well-being," the school said in a statement. "The student is registered as a full-time student at Mississippi Valley State University. University officials are closely monitoring the situation and are committed to providing appropriate support as circumstances develop."

A spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security, under which ICE operates, said in an email that Pang entered the U.S. legally on Nov. 17, 2023 on a temporary basis not to exceed Sept. 5, 2024, but remained in the country beyond that date.

"He accepted voluntary departure and will remain in ICE custody pending removal," the email read. "This administration will not ignore the rule of law."

Pang spent the last two seasons at Monroe University in New York before transferring to Mississippi Valley State. The 6-foot-9 Pang averaged 7.3 points and 3.8 rebounds at Monroe.

In the Seck case, the judge found that she was not a danger to the community or a flight risk, Alsalman said Thursday.

The judge also ruled that she can continue working toward her degree and praised her for her academic and athletic achievements.

The 26-year-old Seck was detained on Aug. 7 at Louisville's Muhammad Ali International Airport as she was planning to travel with her team to a tournament.

The DHS previously said in a statement that Seck legally entered the United States in 2019, then "chose to overstay her welcome in violation of our nation's laws." The agency wrote that an immigration judge had ordered Seck removed a year ago after she failed to appear at an immigration hearing.

Alsalman had previously said that the immigration judge found that Seck did not receive the notice of the prior proceedings.

She was named to the Southern Intercollegiate Athletic Conference all-conference third team last season after she led her team with 11.7 points and 7.3 rebounds. The 6-foot-4 center had five double-doubles last season and scored a season-high 30 points against Lane College on Jan. 14.

Seck also was named the SIAC Women's Basketball Elite 16 award winner. The award is the SIAC's highest academic honor and is presented to student-athletes who demonstrate exemplary performance in sports and the classroom.

images.caption: HBCU basketball player Aminata Seck released from ICE custody on bail

articles.title: Mavs' Kyrie Irving Hypes Cooper Flagg Partnership, 'Looking Forward to Growing with Him'
articles.summary: Dallas Mavericks star Kyrie Irving is excited to begin playing alongside Cooper Flagg ahead of the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
Dallas Mavericks star Kyrie Irving is excited to begin playing alongside Cooper Flagg ahead of the 2026-27 season.

"I'm looking forward to growing with him and seeing how his development happens over the next few years," Irving said Thursday, per Grant Afseth of Dallas Hoops Journal.

The nine-time All-Star is preparing to make his return after missing the entire 2025-26 season while recovering from a torn ACL that he suffered in March 2025.

Flagg put together a stellar inaugural year in Irving's absence, averaging 21.0 points, 6.7 rebounds, 4.5 assists and 1.2 steals per game on 46.8/29.5/82.7 shooting splits.

He earned Rookie of the Year honors for his efforts.

While Irving's on-court impact following the ACL tear is unknown, he should still be able to take some defensive attention off Flagg.

After all, the 34-year-old recorded 24.7 points and 4.6 assists per game while shooting 47.3 percent from the field and 40.1 percent from three-point territory during his shortened 2024-25 campaign.

Irving continued to thrive in one-on-one situations that year, as his 5.4 points per game in isolation ranked No. 5 among all players (via NBA.com ).

Flagg was also looking forward to sharing the floor with the veteran.

"Whatever ends up happening, I'm just excited whenever we get to share the court for the first time," Flagg told reporters. "Obviously it's been an incredible training camp to play together and figure that out on the fly. It's been fun and I'm really excited. Just sharing the court with someone like him and his gravity. The way he can manipulate the game is obviously going to make my life a lot easier."

While Irving has been the subject of trade rumors , he currently remains with Dallas and is set to make his first appearance since the injury during a preseason clash with the Houston Rockets in China on Sunday.

articles.title: NBA Pushes Back on Reports Saying Salary Cap's 2nd Apron Hurts 'Lower' and 'Middle' Class Players
articles.summary: The NBA is pushing back on reports that the second-apron cap rules are having a negative impact on the non-superstar players.
articles.body:
The NBA is pushing back on reports that the second-apron cap rules are having a negative impact on the non-superstar players.

In a statement released on Friday, the league said roster sizes have remained the same and salaries have increased by approximately 30 percent for "all classes of players" since the apron rules were implemented.

The NBA adopted the second-apron system in the most recent collective bargaining agreement that went into effect after the 2023-24 season.

It was designed to limit the financial and roster flexibility for the highest-spending teams. Penalties for going over the second apron include being unable to acquire players via sign-and-trade; and no aggregating contracts for salary-matching in potential trades.

The situation came up earlier in the week when Bruce Brown told Stefan Bondy of the New York Post he received very little interest in free agency with teams citing "the second apron" as the reason.

Brown signed an Exhibit 9 contract with the New York Knicks on Sept. 16. An Exhibit 9 contract is a one-year, non-guaranteed deal that doesn't count against a team's cap until the start of the regular season.

Brown appeared in all 82 games with the Denver Nuggets last season, averaging 7.9 points on 38.5 percent three-point shooting. He has also been a versatile defensive player throughout his career.

This system has absolutely changed the way teams do business. New York Knicks governor James Dolan, whose team just won the NBA title, said days after they clinched the championship he won't spend into the second apron.

That's impacting multiple Knicks players right now after the team confirmed to ESPN's Shams Charania they are tabling all extension talks going into the 2026-27 season.

Karl-Anthony Towns has said he is willing to take a pay cut on an extension with the Knicks, but he finds what they offering to be unfair relative to his value. Josh Hart and Miles McBride are also looking for new deals.

The Oklahoma City Thunder traded key role players like Lu Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins this summer with the max rookie extensions for Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren set to kick in.

Even Victor Wembanyama had to go through a negotiation with the San Antonio Spurs on his rookie extension. He agreed to the 25 percent max extension instead of the potential 30 percent supermax.

Those players like Wembanyama and Towns are marquee names and perennial All-Stars, so lower-level players are likely feeling some trickle-down effect.

David Kelly—executive director of the National Basketball Players Association— said in July, following Wembanyama's contract extension, the system has made it so players have to "carry all of that burden" for trying to keep a team together.

Given the frequent discussion about the second apron and its limitations, it will be interesting to see what, if any, future changes are made during the next round of CBA negotiations.

The current CBA runs through the 2029-30 season, but there is a mutual opt-out after the 2028-29 campaign.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham Calls Out 'Thirsty' Critics in Video Ahead of 2027 WNBA Free Agency
articles.summary: Ahead of her potential foray into WNBA free agency, Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham addressed her detractors on Friday.
articles.body:
Ahead of her potential foray into WNBA free agency, Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham addressed her detractors on Friday.

Speaking during the latest episode of No Hesitation with Sophie Cunningham and Drew Hanlen (beginning at the 2:30 mark of the podcast) , Cunningham suggested that she is no longer concerning herself with fan criticism:

"That's why I literally don't even care what anyone says about me anymore," Cunningham said. "I've said this so many times, if you're going to live by the praise, you're going to die by the hate. The majority of these people have never picked up a ball in their entire lives, and they're just, like, thirsty to have attention or be relevant in some type of way. No matter what anyone says to me, I'm gonna continue to do me. I know what I bring to the table. It's not always in the stat sheet. So for you to not say I'm effective or any of that, whatever. Suck it."

Cunningham, 30, is an eight-year WNBA veteran who has spent the past two seasons with the Fever, following a six-year run as a member of the Phoenix Mercury.

She started a career-low three of the 43 games she appeared in for Indiana this past season, but she was a key contributor off the bench nonetheless, averaging 7.9 points, 2.3 rebounds, 1.6 three-pointers made and 1.2 assists per game.

Cunningham's biggest contribution was her work from behind the arc, as she shot 41.9 percent from distance, which ranked fifth in the WNBA season.

She has shot 40 percent or better from downtown in a season four times in her career, which figures to make her a sought-after commodity on the free-agent market by the Fever or potentially even a different team.

The Fever's 2026 season came to an end last week when they fell to the Las Vegas Aces in Game 3 of their first-round playoff series.

Star players Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston are under contract for Indiana next season, but Cunningham is eligible for free agency, as is four-time All-Star guard Kelsey Mitchell.

If one or both of Cunningham and Mitchell sign elsewhere, the Fever could have a much different look next season, even with Clark and Boston still in the fold.

articles.title: Kevin Durant Says He Thought Russell Westbrook Had '5 or 6 More Years Left' Before NBA Retirement
articles.summary: Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant was apparently taken by surprise when his former teammate Russell Westbrook announced his retirement from the NBA this August.
articles.body:
Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant was apparently taken by surprise when his former teammate Russell Westbrook announced his retirement from the NBA this August.

"I was a little sad, because I still thought Russ had five or six more years left," Durant told reporters Friday after kicking off the preseason with a win over Dallas Mavericks in China. "He has an athletic body that can still impact the game positively.

"But sometimes, people are at that point where they just want to step away and do something different. So, congrats to him on an iconic career, and I know the next phase in his life he's gonna put the same amount of work into just like he did in basketball."

Westbrook averaged 15.2 points, 5.4 rebounds and 6.7 assists per game while playing 29 minutes per night last season for the Sacramento Kings.

The 37-year-old announced his retirement after 18 seasons, eight of which he spent playing alongside Durant on the Oklahoma City Thunder, in August.

Durant, who turned 38 in September, is preparing for his 19th NBA season, and his first without Westbrook in the league since his rookie year.

He is currently signed through this season with the Rockets with a 2027-28 player option on which he can decide by next June.

Durant said in September he doesn't want to reduce his minutes this season after averaging more than 36 per night as a 78-game starter in his first campaign with the Rockets.

After missing most of the Rockets' first-round series loss last spring, Durant will hope for better injury luck as he heads into his second season in Houston.

articles.title: Russell Westbrook Wants to Be LA Olympics 2028 Torchbearer After NBA Retirement
articles.summary: Former NBA star guard Russell Westbrook wants to carry the Olympic torch in two years, when the 2028 Summer Olympics will be held in Los Angeles.
articles.body:
Former NBA star guard Russell Westbrook wants to carry the Olympic torch in two years, when the 2028 Summer Olympics will be held in Los Angeles.

Westbrook made his comments Friday, per LoJo Media.

"I'm putting this out now: I want to be in the presentation of Los Angeles, as it pertains to carrying the torch during the 2028 Olympics," Westbrook said (h/t ESPN's Ben Golliver ) on Friday, when the Los Angeles City Council honored the nine-time All-Star for his community service efforts.

Westbrook, who was born and raised in Los Angeles and attended UCLA for a year before joining the NBA in 2008, founded the Why Not? Foundation in 2012.

"The Russell Westbrook Why Not? Foundation aims to create pathways of empowerment for underserved communities in the areas of educational opportunities, workforce development and accessible mental health resources," the foundation's website reads.

"With 'Why Not?' being a personal ignition for Russell Westbrook, the foundation looks to instill this mindset in the youth while offering their resources to set children and their communities up for continued success."

Westbrook enjoyed a great 18-year career, averaging 20.9 points, 8.0 assists, 6.9 rebounds and 1.6 steals per game. He's a nine-time All-NBA player, three-time assist leader, two-time scoring champion and the 2016-17 NBA MVP. Westbrook also averaged a triple-double on four different occasions.

He made a great impact on the court (especially for the Oklahoma City Thunder from 2008-2019) and is now a member of the NBA's 75th Anniversary Team.

In the present date, it's clear Westbrook wants to carry the Olympic torch. He elaborated more, per Golliver.

"To be able to [carry the torch], you have to be able to position yourself to have your hands in so many different areas," he said. "For me, I'm working religiously impacting so many people, advancing technology, energy, education, health care, mental health and wellness. Every aspect, I want to have my hands in to help any way I can."

Per a United States Olympic and Paralympic Committee press release , the torch relay will begin in the spring of 2028 in Atlanta, where the last Summer Olympics in the United States were held in 1996.

articles.title: Warriors, Knicks, Lakers Top Sportico's 2026 List of NBA's Most Valuable Teams
articles.summary: The New York Knicks followed up their 2026 NBA title by leapfrogging the Los Angeles Lakers in Sportico's annual list of the most valuable NBA franchises.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks followed up their 2026 NBA title by leapfrogging the Los Angeles Lakers in Sportico 's annual list of the most valuable NBA franchises.

The Knicks' valuation rose by 30 percent over the last year to $12.8 billion, ranking behind only the Golden State Warriors' valuation of $14.5 billion, according to Sportico.

The Lakers ($12.5 billion valuation) join those two franchises as the only NBA teams with valuation in the 11 digits, per Sportico. The franchise could set an NBA record if a pending sale at that valuation is approved.

Only the Dallas Cowboys ($15.5 billion valuation) were listed as a more valuable global sports franchise than the Warriors in Sportico's annual rankings, per Sportico's Kurt Badenhausen .

The valuations are based on team revenue as well as other revenue sources tied to each franchise, including WNBA teams and arena ownership, according to Sportico.

The Chicago Bulls and Miami Heat tied for the NBA lead in one-year value increase with jumps of 33 percent each, per Sportico.

Those two clubs now rank among the top six NBA teams with projected valuations of over $8 billion each, according to Sportico.

The Philadelphia 76ers, which ranked ninth after a year-by-year value increase of 27 percent brought the franchise's valuation to $7.15 billion, could be hoping to see a larger spike after signing LeBron James this offseason.

NBA clubs in the top half of the rankings overall saw their valuations increase by an average of 26 percent over the last year, according to Sportico.

Four teams earned Sportico valuations of $4.5 billion or less in the Minnesota Timberwolves, Portland Trail Blazers, New Orleans Pelicans and Memphis Grizzlies.

These bottom-four franchises each saw valuation increases of six percent or less over the past year, per Sportico.

Badenhausen noted "revenue for the 2026-27 NBA season might be choppy" because of the ceasing of operations of the company that ran local broadcasts under the name FanDuel Sports Network.

Teams impacted by changes in media right deals could lean on the NBA's revenue-sharing rules, through which top clubs and luxury tax proceeds distribute revenue to the league's less lucrative teams, Badenhausen noted.

articles.title: Texas legend has sky-high hopes for Longhorns ahead of Red River Rivalry game vs Oklahoma
articles.summary: Colt McCoy calls the Texas Longhorns' current roster arguably the most talented ever as they enter the Red River Rivalry ranked No. 1 at 4-0.
articles.body: The Red River Rivalry makes its return on Saturday, and someone all too familiar with the big game was back in Dallas on Friday gearing up for his former Texas Longhorns to continue their national title hopes. Colt McCoy never quite reached the promised land in Austin, but he did have the upper hand in the matchup, going 3-1 in his four years, including the 45-35 victory when his Texas squad was fifth in the country, and the Oklahoma Sooners were ranked No. 1. Texas has won three of the last four matchups after losing 10 of the previous 13, including the 2018 Big 12 Championship Game. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD "Just the history of this game, right in the middle between both schools, played in Dallas, played in the Cotton Bowl, that place, I mean, you just feel the sanctity of that place when you walk down the tunnel, the shared tunnel. The fans are split down the middle, it's always played in October, it's kind of the kickoff into your conference," McCoy said to Fox News Digital in an interview Friday. "It's just a really, really special game, at least the ones that I was a part of. "And the beauty of rivalries is that you may be the best team in the country, but if you don't strap it up and play that day or if you're off that day, like you got problems. So, I love it. Just being back here is pretty surreal. It's a really, really fun weekend." McCoy was hanging out with some fans on behalf of Fanatics, which offers official Red River Rivalry merchandise. "I had a great time, man. Texas fans are the best, dude. They show up everywhere. It's a whole lot of fun to engage with them. And then especially this weekend, this was the one game on your calendar every year that you circled, and you thought about, and you got nervous about all the things. This is a fun one," McCoy said. "Fanatics is great. Listen, it's a wonderful brand. The gear is incredible. The fans showed out. There was like a million fans in the Texas line and nobody on the Oklahoma side. So, this is exactly what I wanted." McCoy admitted that it was tough to stay focused on the game before the Red River Rivalry knowing what was soon on the table. "Generally, we didn't play great if I can remember right," McCoy said (he went 3-1 in games preceding the rivalry, the loss being a 41-21 upset by unranked Kansas State when they were No. 7). "But then the moment you get back in the locker room after that game, they've got Boomer Sooner playing and they play it all week, and by the time you get to the game, you're just ready to punch somebody in the mouth." But when McCoy was a third-round pick in the NFL Draft, he had no choice but to throw the rivalry aside. "I got to admit, I've had some amazing teammates that came out of Oklahoma over the years. Trent Williams for a long time, he is a phenomenal teammate. He may be the greatest left tackle ever. Still playing 17 years at an All-Pro level. It really is unbelievable. A great guy, great friend. Played with Adrian Peterson for a couple years, Tress Way, amazing punter. Kyler Murray is my boy. So, there's unfortunately been some really good dudes come out of Oklahoma." But now that he's out of the game, it's all Texas and no Oklahoma once again, and he feels like this year's squad has what it takes to bring home its first national title in over two decades. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "Listen, we're 4-0 and number one in the country, and they hadn't really clicked yet, right? The sky's the limit for this team. They're super talented. They're well coached. They kind of have all the makings from both sides of the ball to be really special. And I certainly think that they have a lot of confidence internally, and they just got to go do it. And I really think they will," said McCoy. "We had a 10-year dry spell that was hard. I think right now what I'll give you is I do think that this is arguably the most talented roster that Texas has had. Just when you look across the board, you look at the coaching staff, you look at the players, you look at just the straight talent, like man-to-man, they're never going to go into a game and be outmatched. And that really got to give everyone on that team a lot of confidence." SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

articles.title: WNBA Addresses Liberty Timeout Controversy After Dream's Game 2 Win in Semifinal Bracket
articles.summary: The WNBA says a "misunderstanding" led to New York Liberty star Breanna Stewart saying she was incorrectly informed about whether her team had a reset timeout remaining late in a Game 2 semifinals loss to the Atlanta Dream.
articles.body:
The WNBA says a "misunderstanding" led to New York Liberty star Breanna Stewart saying she was incorrectly informed about whether her team had a reset timeout remaining late in a Game 2 semifinals loss to the Atlanta Dream.

Stewart said after the game she had been told by referees the Liberty did not have the option to reset shortly before her team conceded a 101-98 overtime loss without having taken the timeout.

A WNBA spokesperson said in a statement provided to ESPN's Alexa Philippou it was "clear on video and audio" Stewart had asked official Kevin Fahy about the timeout.

Cunningham's Take on Timeout Controversy 🤬

"At that moment, there were multiple overlapping conversations and non-verbal exchanges between the referees, game participants, and also Stewart with Liberty bench personnel, which led to a misunderstanding amongst the various parties," the WNBA spokesperson said, per Philippou.

"Our referees can certainly handle these interactions better and have been given that feedback. No further follow up is expected on the situation at this time."

Video footage captured by ESPN shared by the New York Post showed Stewart talking to an official as the Dream's Angel Reese was preparing to take free throws with 4.3 seconds left in overtime, then later turning to address the Liberty's bench.

The WNBA introduced reset timeouts, which allows teams to make substitutions and advance to the frontcourt but not huddle, ahead of the 2024 season. Teams are entitled to one reset timeout in the final two minutes of either a fourth quarter or overtime period, according to the league .

Stewart initially told reporters she had asked Fahy if her team had a reset timeout, and he had told her he was "going to check at the table."

She said Fahy then looked to referee Fatou Cissoko-Stephens, who answered negatively, at which point he told Stewart the Liberty didn't have the timeout.

Liberty head coach Chris DeMarco agreed he had also been told his team did not have a reset timeout.

When asked about the situation in a postgame pool report, an official said Stewart had been "standing behind referee Fahy when he confirmed with his partner between Reese's penalty free throws that New York did indeed have a reset timeout remaining," per USA Today's Meghan L. Hall .

The official also said there was no conversation between referees and Liberty staff, according to Hall.

Stewart indicated ahead of Game 3 she felt the situation could erode trust between players, the referees and the league.

"You want to have respect between players and refs, and players and the league, and all of these things, and in order to have respect, you need to build trust," Stewart said (h/t ESPN's Kareem Copeland). "And building trust comes with being honest. Putting me in a position to question my integrity is really disappointing."

Stewart and the Liberty tipped off their must-win Game 3 against the Dream at 7:30 p.m. ET.

Fahy and Cissoko-Stephens will not be officiating the contest, although they will be in action in another semifinal Game 3 later tonight when the Golden State Valkyries look to advance past the Las Vegas Aces at 9:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown Drops Viral Quote on Facing Celtics for 1st Time Since Blockbuster 76ers Trade
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown discussed how he feels heading into a matchup with the Boston Celtics, his former team, after experiencing a change of scenery in the offseason.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown discussed how he feels heading into a matchup with the Boston Celtics, his former team, after experiencing a change of scenery in the offseason.

"It's just life," Brown said on a live stream. "It's like running into your ex out in public like, 'Dang, we used to go together.' And you just look at them and be like, 'Dang.' You just gotta go about your business."

On July 1, the Celtics traded Brown to the 76ers in exchange for Paul George, two first-round draft picks and two second-round picks.

Boston and Philadelphia are set to face off in a preseason clash on Saturday.

Brown spent the first 10 seasons of his career with the Celtics after they selected him with the No. 3 overall pick in the 2016 NBA draft.

He steadily blossomed into a top offensive option for Boston, earning five All-Star nods and two All-NBA selections throughout his tenure as a member of the organization.

Brown also helped the Celtics win the 2024 NBA Finals, earning Finals MVP honors for his efforts.

He became Boston's leading scorer during its 2025-26 campaign while Jayson Tatum recovered from a torn Achilles , averaging a career-high 28.7 points per game on 47.7/34.7/79.5 shooting splits.

After the Celtics suffered a first-round exit in the playoffs, they reportedly offered Brown in trade packages for two-time MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo.

After the Milwaukee Bucks ultimately sent Antetokounmpo to the Miami Heat, Boston started to field offers for Brown from other teams.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Brown never requested a trade before he was dealt to the 76ers.

Now, the 29-year-old is set to return to TD Garden for the first time since the swap. Tip-off between the Celtics and 76ers on Saturday is at 8 p.m. ET.

articles.title: 'F--ked Up,' Jaylen Brown Reacts to Anthony Edwards Trolling Him, LeBron James in Viral Adidas Video
articles.summary: Jaylen Brown is unimpressed by the apparent jabs Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards took toward him and his Philadelphia 76ers teammate LeBron James as part of an ad campaign with adidas.
articles.body:
Jaylen Brown is unimpressed by the apparent jabs Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards took toward him and his Philadelphia 76ers teammate LeBron James as part of an ad campaign with adidas.

Brown reacted to the commercial, in which Edwards seemingly joked about Brown's hair , in a Friday Twitch stream with Sixers guard VJ Edgecombe.

"That's f--ked up. AE, I thought you was my boy," Brown said. "Come on, man, that's crazy. We ain't doing that."

Brown continued, "Adidas wrote this for you, my boy? They wrote this for you? They're trying to drive a wedge between us."

Edwards started out his commercial by referencing James signing with the 76ers this offseason in free agency.

"He was gon' join me in Minnesota, but I guess his knees couldn't handle the cold weather," Edwards joked.

Edwards continued, "We know why he really made that decision. Philly got some of the best barbers in the world. Between him and ol' boy from Boston, they're gonna have a whole lot of enhancements going on in that locker room."

This isn't the first time Brown has responded to trolling from Edwards, who also named Brown as the player he wouldn't want to date his sister during All-Star weekend in February.

Brown could now have a new point of contention to discuss with Edwards when the Timberwolves and 76ers meet for the first time this season in January.

articles.title: Olivia Rodrigo Attends Liberty vs. Angel Reese, Dream WNBA Playoff Game in Trending Video
articles.summary: Singer-songwriter and three-time Grammy Award winner Olivia Rodrigo attended Game 3 of the WNBA semifinal series between the host New York Liberty and the visiting Atlanta Dream on Friday evening at Brooklyn's Barclays Center.
articles.body:
Singer-songwriter and three-time Grammy Award winner Olivia Rodrigo attended Game 3 of the WNBA semifinal series between the host New York Liberty and the visiting Atlanta Dream on Friday evening at Brooklyn's Barclays Center.

During a second-quarter timeout, the jumbotron above the court captured Rodrigo holding a Liberty jersey with her name and No. 10 on the back. Rodrigo greeted the thousands of fans, who cheered the star in return.

Cunningham's Take on Timeout Controversy 🤬

The No. 8 seed Liberty entered the best-of-five series down 2-0 to the No. 4 seed Dream after Atlanta won the first two games, 92-82 and 101-98 (in overtime), respectively. The Dream completed the sweep Friday, defeating the Liberty 85-83 to make the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013.

articles.title: Angel Reese, Ionescu's Box Score Stats, Highlights as Dream Eliminate Liberty in WNBA Playoffs
articles.summary: Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream are off to the 2026 WNBA Finals after ending a historic playoff run for Sabrina Ionescu and the New York Liberty.
articles.body:
Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream are off to the 2026 WNBA Finals after ending a historic playoff run for Sabrina Ionescu and the New York Liberty.

Rhyne Howard and Jordin Canada led the Dream on a fourth-quarter comeback to seal an 85-83 win over Liberty in Friday night's Game 3 of the semifinals.

Here's a look at the top stats and highlights from the victory that sent the Dream to the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013.

Cunningham's Take on Timeout Controversy 🤬

The Dream jumped out to an early lead at Barclays Center in large part thanks to Reese, who drained a pair of three-pointers while recording 10 points in a postseason quarter for the first time in her WNBA career (h/t ESPN's Alexa Philippou ).

Reese's hot start helped the Dream hold a seven-point lead after 10 minutes, but the visitors fell behind after getting outscored 50-41 over the next two quarters.

Tensions rose as Reese shared heated exchanges with Ionescu and Jonquel Jones late in the first half.

The Liberty went into the fourth quarter with a two-point lead thanks in part to a trio of three-pointers by Ionescu.

Ionsecu helped her team pull further ahead by splashing her fourth of the night early in the fourth quarter. That allowed Ionescu to pass Kara Lawson for 11th on the WNBA's postseason three-pointer leaderboard, per ClutchPoints .

The Liberty were unable to hold on to that advantage long enough to extend their postseason.

Rhyne Howard and Jordin Canada led the Dream on a 7-0 run to take back the lead with under five minutes remaining in the fourth. Atlanta then held onto the advantage to close out the elimination win.

The Liberty made history by sweeping the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx from the first round of the 2026 playoffs.

The 2024 champions will now head home while the Dream prepare to play for what could be the franchise's first WNBA championship against either the Golden State Valkyries or the Las Vegas Aces.

The Valkyries hold a 2-0 lead in their own semifinal series, in which the Aces are playing to extend their postseason Friday in Las Vegas.

articles.title: Angel Reese Reacts to Making 1st WNBA Finals After Dream Eliminate Liberty From Playoff Bracket
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese has advanced to the 2026 WNBA Finals almost exactly one year after announcing she was manifesting that accomplishment.
articles.body:
Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese has advanced to the 2026 WNBA Finals almost exactly one year after announcing she was manifesting that accomplishment.

"I manifested this. When I came to Atlanta, I knew what I was getting," Reese said after the Dream clinched a Finals berth with an 85-83 win over the New York Liberty in Friday night's Game 3 of the semifinals.

Reese continued, "This team has poured so much into me. We poured so much into each other. I posted and Tweeted, 10/10/25, that I was manifesting the Finals, and this is my moment. I'm supposed to be here. I thank God for this moment."

Reese was referencing a post she shared on social media the day the Las Vegas Aces won the 2025 title over the Phoenix Mercury.

She later explained why she made that post while speaking with reporters after the win:

"I was watching the game... I've sat at home for the last two years and watched it. And I kept saying, I texted [Kahleah Copper] and I was like... give me one game in the playoffs and have an opportunity to come to Atlanta. Them wanting me in Atlanta and being able to push me every day to help me get to this very moment it's really a shout out to them. I manifest a lot of things. I think it's important to speak positives into your life, positive into your team. But this is all God. I'm just so thankful and I'm blessed to be able to be in a situation a lot of people wish they were here and I'm not gonna take this moment for granted. I'm here for a reason, we're all here for a reason. In chapel today they talked about the moment, being able to maximize the moment. And we have a very praying crew group. Eight out of the 12 of our players go to chapel, and we take that seriously. So I'm just really happy about the girls that are just in that locker room. It's just really a blessing to be around them."

Reese will now cap off her WNBA postseason debut with her own trip to the championship series. The 24-year-old told reporters after the game that "the job is not done" and the Dream are "not satisfied" by just making it to the Finals.

She started out Friday's elimination game by scoring 10 points in a quarter for the first time in her postseason career, per ESPN's Alexa Philippou .

That scoring outburst included a pair of three-pointers. The Dream are now 13-0 in games during which Reese scores from deep, per ESPN Insights.

Reese finished the game with a team-high 22 points on 7-for-18 shooting from the field to go along with nine rebounds, three assists, two blocks and a steal.

She has now racked up the most steals and blocks in a single postseason by any center making their first WNBA playoff appearance, per Polymarket Hoops .

Reese was traded from the Chicago Sky to the Dream in exchange for a package including two first-round picks in April.

The Sky won a total of 23 games over two seasons with Reese before the trade, after which Reese said she had come to Atlanta to win a title.

Reese went on to win the WNBA's Defensive Player of the Year award before assisting in the Dream's first run to the Finals since 2013.

She will now look to cap off her third WNBA season by helping lead the Dream battle for the franchise's first title against either the Golden State Valkyries or Las Vegas Aces. The Valkyries currently hold a 2-0 semifinal lead and could close out their own series Friday night in Las Vegas.

articles.title: Caleb Wilson, Cam Boozer's Final Box Score Stats, Highlights from Grizzlies vs. Bulls Preseason
articles.summary: Caleb Wilson and Cameron Boozer faced off Friday night for the first time since battling in the NBA Summer League.
articles.body:
Caleb Wilson and Cameron Boozer faced off Friday night for the first time since battling in the NBA Summer League.

Wilson hit five three-pointers for the Chicago Bulls during a 104-100 preseason loss to Boozer and the Memphis Grizzlies.

Here's a look at how both 2026 lottery picks fared in Chicago as the lead-up to their respective rookie seasons continued.

Boozer shone for the Grizzlies in a first half highlighted by his second-quarter dunk.

He went into the break having gone 3-for-5 from the field with 10 points, four rebounds and three assists.

Wilson was less active in the first half, during which he went 0-for-2 from the field while contributing three rebounds and one point.

He exploded in the third quarter, splashing a trio of three-pointers while racking up 12 points, a rebound and a steal.

Wilson later led a comeback push by getting the Bulls within two points of tying the game with a clutch three-pointer in the final minute.

He closed out the preseason loss having shot 7-for-17 from the field and 5-for-11 from deep.

Wilson will have three more opportunities to get preseason playing time over the next week.

The Bulls are set for upcoming exhibition matchups against the Denver Nuggets, Milwaukee Bucks and Minnesota Timberwolves before opening the regular season Oct. 21 at the Toronto Raptors.

The Grizzlies begin the regular season by welcoming the Utah Jazz to town the same day. Boozer and his teammates will first wrap up the preseason next Friday versus the Charlotte Hornets.

articles.title: Dream sweep Liberty on Angel Reese's 22 points, head to first WNBA Finals since 2013
articles.summary: After three consecutive first-round playoff exits, Atlanta returns to the WNBA Finals for the first time in 13 seasons.
articles.body: The Atlanta Dream are in the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013 with an 85-83 win over the New York Liberty in Game 3 of their playoff semifinals series.Angel Reese scored 22 points — 18 in the first half — with 9 rebounds, 3 assists and 2 blocks in a tough battle with New York's Jonquel Jones to lead the Dream. Rhyne Howard followed with 21 points, and Jordin Canada was the second-half catalyst for Atlanta, finishing with 19 points and 11 assists.Atlanta finished the first quarter with a 25-18 lead, but the Liberty fought back fiercely, playing like a team whose season was at stake. Jones, battling near the basket with Reese, along with Sabrina Ionescu getting fired up by a non-call on a push-off by Isobel Borlase, ignited the Barclays Center crowd. The Liberty rode that surge to rally from a 12-point deficit in the third quarter to eventually take the lead after a 17-4 run. Jones scored 26 points for the Liberty on 11-for-17 shooting from the floor to go with 14 rebounds and 3 blocks. Breanna Stewart also finished with 26 points after only tallying 8 points in the first half. Sabrina Ionescu added 12 points, shooting 4-for-11 on 3-pointers. Stewart hit all 13 of her free throws, while grabbing 4 rebounds, dishing out 6 assists and blocking 2 shots. But she missed a baseline jumper that could have tied the score with 9.9 seconds remaining. This is the first time Stewart has been on a team that was swept out of the WNBA playoffs. The Dream played without Allisha Gray, who sat out with a left hand injury for the second consecutive game. Gray went through pregame warmups, but determined she could not go. Smesko said the team was being cautious, looking ahead to the remainder of the playoffs.Dream ascending, Liberty descendingAtlanta advancing to the Finals continues an impressive two-year turnaround under head coach Karl Smesko. The Dream finished with 30-14 records in each of the past two seasons, but took that next step with the blockbuster trade for Reese before the season."The job is not done," Reese said in a postgame press conference. "We're definitely happy about where we are right now, but we're not satisfied."Angel Reese:"The job is not done...we're not satisfied" pic.twitter.com/Zok2D3IjaE— Oh No He Didn't (@ohnohedidnt24) October 10, 2026 Meanwhile, the Liberty finished as the No. 8 seed in the WNBA playoffs with a 26-18 record. They upset the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx in the first round, but getting swept out of the postseason is a bad look for a team with stars like Stewart, Jones and Ionescu on its roster. The exit is even more notable when Sandy Brondello was fired as head coach after last season's first-round exit — one year after winning the WNBA championship — and Chris DeMarco was hired to presumably get better results. "I don't think we were consistent," Stewart said after the game. "This is not cramming for a test. You gotta be ready to go and ready to go from the jump." The Dream will face the Golden State Valkyries in the WNBA Finals after they knocked off the Las Vegas Aces in a Game 3 sweep of their own. Game 1 is Saturday, Oct. 17 at 3:30 p.m. ET. Follow along with live updates, highlights and news from the Dream's Game 3 win over the Liberty to close out their WNBA semifinals series:

articles.title: WNBA Finals 2026 Set, 3 Instant Reactions to Dream vs. Valkyries on the Bracket
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream qualified for the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013 after completing their three-game semifinal sweep of the New York Liberty with an 85-83 road victory.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream qualified for the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013 after completing their three-game semifinal sweep of the New York Liberty with an 85-83 road victory.

Later in the evening, the Golden State Valkyries, in their second season, made the Finals for the first time after knocking the defending WNBA champion Las Vegas Aces out of the playoffs with an 87-77 overtime win to complete their own three-game semifinal sweep.

Here's a look at three instant reactions:

Four-time All-Star guard Allisha Gray's importance to this team can't be overstated. The 10-year veteran averaged a team-high 19.0 points on 46.3 percent shooting, started all 44 games and averaged 32.6 minutes per game. Gray also scored 22 points in Games 1 and 2 of the Dream's two-game sweep of the Washington Mystics in the first round.

Unfortunately, Gray suffered a finger injury on her left (shooting) hand in Game 1 of the semifinal series against the Liberty and played just 11 minutes. She missed Game 2 and was questionable for Game 3 before ultimately sitting. A pregame appearance Friday provided some hope.

Her absence certainly cast doubt on the Dream's chances, especially against a talented, star-laden Liberty team that crushed the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx in a first-round sweep.

However, Atlanta beat New York 101-98 in overtime in Game 2 and then finished the sweep in Game 3.

In essence, the Dream ran a super-short six-woman rotation, putting DeWanna Bonner in the lineup and then playing the starters as much as they could handle.

Angel Reese led Atlanta in scoring (22 points, nine rebounds), Jordin Canada paced the team in assists (13 dimes alongside 19 points) and DeWanna Bonner dominated the boards (13-point, 13-rebound double-double). Rhyne Howard added 21 points, while Isobel Borlase scored 10 off the bench.

The Dream led 51-39 in the third quarter but saw that edge fade. A quick 5-0 run midway through the fourth quarter gave the Dream a 75-71 edge, and Atlanta kept New York at bay from there.

The hope, of course, is that Gray can return soon enough. The good news is that the Finals don't start until next Saturday, so she has seven-plus days to recover. That will be a huge boost for Atlanta, which proved it can persevere without the star in big games. Adding Gray back is a major win, though, especially against the WNBA's best defense.

Golden State Plays Beautiful, Composed Basketball

Golden State was tough, tenacious, aggressive, fierce, and out-hustled and out-worked the Aces in this series, but especially in the Game 3 finale. The Valkyries were down 47-36 in the third quarter but bore down and went on a 17-0 run. The two teams went back-and-forth for the rest of the second half, but overtime arrived after Aces star Chelsea Gray's mid-range jumper went in-and-out at the regulation buzzer.

Golden State didn't flinch in overtime. The Valkyries showcased their brand of basketball, playing perfect defense and making great plays on offense. They executed amazing passes and cuts, hit clutch open shots and just played great team basketball. Golden State ultimately outscored Las Vegas 17-7 in overtime.

The Valkyries' team-first, defensive brand of basketball and great depth showed up. The team with the league's most efficient defense featured 10 players on the court, all of whom played at least seven minutes (seven played 17 or more).

Eight players scored six or more points, led by Kayla Thornton's 18. Active hands led to 12 steals (Defensive Player of the Year runner-up Gabby Williams and Cecilia Zandalasini each had three), and five-time WNBA MVP/Aces center A'ja Wilson shot just 6-of-19. The Aces' backcourt of Gray and Jackie Young committed 11 turnovers.

Head coach Natalie Nakase has done an unbelievable job, and she's earned recognition as one of the best coaches in American professional sports.

The Valkyries showcase their incredible grit, toughness, and chemistry nightly, and they did so again here.

The first- and second-best defensive teams (by efficiency) will now play in the WNBA Finals.

In one corner, you have the league's deepest team, a squad that has used its tremendous defense, depth, and chemistry to vault itself to the championship round in two short years. The Valkyries will enjoy home-court advantage in this championship series, a huge boost for a team that's gone 21-5 in San Francisco this year (including playoffs).

In the other corner, you have the WNBA's hottest team. The Dream were 13-10 just after the regular season's halfway point, but they've won 22 of their last 26 games, including 10 in a row (14 of 15). Atlanta also crushed teams down the stretch from the back end of the regular season through Game 1 of the semifinals. The Dream's last 13 regular season wins and first three playoff wins (all games Gray played in) were by seven or more points.

Golden State had the major edge in the regular season, sweeping Atlanta 3-0 and winning the games by a combined 19 points (77-66, 78-75, 88-83). However, Atlanta is scorching-hot right now. Presuming Gray is ready for the WNBA Finals, the Dream should give Golden State a great challenge.

A key here, though, is Bonner, who hasn't played Golden State as a member of the Dream. Bonner joined the Dream via free agency after her old team, the Phoenix Mercury, bought out her contract. Atlanta is 10-0 with Bonner on the floor, and her semifinal efforts, sans Gray, clearly helped the Dream advance to the Finals.

Overall, expect a hard-fought classic that goes six or seven games. Here's a look at the schedule:

WNBA Finals (Best-of-7, 2-2-1-1-1 Format)

Game 1 (Atlanta at Golden State): 3:30 p.m. ET, NBC/Peacock

Game 2 (Atlanta at Golden State): 8 p.m. ET, USA/Peacock

Game 3 (Golden State at Atlanta): 8 p.m. ET, USA/Peacock

Game 4 (Golden State at Atlanta): 3:30 p.m. ET, NBC/Peacock

Game 5* (Atlanta at Golden State): 8 p.m. ET, USA/Peacock

Game 6* (Golden State at Atlanta): 8 p.m. ET, USA/Peacock

Game 7* (Atlanta at Golden State): 8 p.m. ET, USA/Peacock

articles.title: WNBA playoffs: Valkyries finish sweep of Aces, reach Finals in second year of existence
articles.summary: The 2026 WNBA Finals will be the Valkyries against the Dream after a pair of semifinal sweeps.
articles.body: The Golden State Valkyries finished off a statement sweep of the Las Vegas Aces on Friday.With an 87-77 overtime win on Friday, the Valkyries eliminated the defending champions in the WNBA semifinals. They are headed to the WNBA Finals in their second year of existence.IN JUST THEIR 2ND SEASON, THE GOLDEN STATE VALKYRIES ARE HEADED TO THE WNBA FINALS! pic.twitter.com/XZrBuQpSSN— WNBA on NBC and Peacock (@WNBAonNBC) October 10, 2026 It will be Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream waiting for them. The Dream finished off their own sweep of a championship-winning core earlier in the evening, taking out the New York Liberty in another close game.Whoever wins, it will be the first championship in franchise history. It will also be the first time since 2021 that the Finals haven't featured either the Aces or Liberty.Game 1 is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 17 (NBC/Peacock).It's the continuation of a dream season for the Valkyries, who followed up a highly successful inaugural season in 2025 with the second-best regular-season record in the WNBA at 32-12. From Day 1 under head coach Natalie Nakase, a former Aces assistant, they have leaned into an identity built around relentless defense and a truckload of 3-pointers.That wound up being more than the Aces could handle. The first three halves of play were absolute misery for the defending champions, though they did make Game 2 competitive with a great fourth quarter. They appeared to carry something over from that in Game 3, entering halftime with a nine-point lead that could have been 12 had Chelsea Gray gotten off a buzzer-beating 3-pointer a second earlier.Unfortunately, that momentum drained away not long into the third quarter. The Valkyries ripped off a 17-0 run to grab the lead and then some, and Las Vegas had to play catch-up just to force overtime. Both teams had a chance to score at the end of regulation, but shots from Gabby Williams and Chelsea Gray clanked away.Overtime wound up being one-sided, with Gabby Williams landing the dagger with less than a minute left.GABBY WILLIAMS HITS THE HUGE JUMPER IN OVERTIME AND THE VALKYRIES CAN TASTE A FINALS APPEARANCE! pic.twitter.com/coxQSja0Fc— WNBA on NBC and Peacock (@WNBAonNBC) October 10, 2026 Kayla Thornton led the Valkyries with 18 points on 5-of-12 shooting, plus 9 rebounds, while Williams had 16 points on 16 shots. The biggest factor might have been Kiah Stokes, the defensive-minded center who posted 11 points on 5-of-5 shooting, 10 rebounds, 3 assists, 3 blocks and 2 steals in a team-high 37 minutes.Stokes' real job was clear all series: Don't let A'ja Wilson do GOAT stuff. She was mostly successful, holding the five-time WNBA MVP to 23 points per game on 41.7% shooting plus 7 rebounds and 1 assist per game during the series. Those are solid numbers, but not for Wilson. She had 32 points on 64.6% shooting and 11.7 rebounds per game in her previous series against the Indiana Fever.With Jackie Young dealing with foul trouble on a mediocre shooting night and Chelsea Gray posting 17 points (only two of them after halftime), the Aces didn't have many wells to pull from, especially given their other injuries.It's the first time Las Vegas has been swept since Becky Hammon took over, and the kind of series that begs the question of how many years are left in this window with Wilson at 30 years old.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for all the news, highlights and more from Game 3 of the Valkyries-Aces semifinals series:

articles.title: How Angel Reese manifested her Dream en route to the WNBA Finals: 'We're all here for a reason'
articles.summary: Call her Finals Barbie. Her accessories include "mebounds," a freshly acquired 3-point shot and a vision board come to life.
articles.body:
NEW YORK — Call her Finals Barbie. Her accessories include "mebounds," a freshly acquired 3-point shot and a vision board come to life. On her mind is speaking positivity into her life. One in particular stood out.

"manifesting the finals>>>" she wrote on X the night the Las Vegas Aces clinched the 2025 championship over the Phoenix Mercury.

From dream world to reality, Barbie. And in exactly 364 days and 23 hours. Reese will play in her first WNBA Finals, and the Dream in their first since 2013, after sweeping the 2024 champion New York Liberty in the semifinals . They won Game 3, 85-83, to earn eight days off before the Finals begin on Oct. 17.

"I knew I wanted to be here," Reese said of her ascension. "I knew this moment I'm supposed to be here at this very time."

Reese does not typically share the goals on her vision board, though she divulged at the beginning of the series that it included Defensive Player of the Year . Reaching the playoffs, she said, was technically there, but after a preseason trade from the Chicago Sky to the Atlanta Dream, she had no doubt it was reachable.

That same night of the 2025 Finals, she sent a text to former Sky champion Kahleah Copper, who was on the losing side of the Aces' title sweep.

"I said last year, give me one playoff game, and I'm going to make it to the Finals," Reese said ahead of Game 3. "And I'm here now."

The No. 4 Dream are 5-0 in the playoffs after a sweep of the No. 5 Washington Mystics, a young group that outperformed its stature, and the No. 8 New York Liberty, a veteran one that underperformed its talent. It's largely on the back of Reese, a player Dream head coach Karl Smesko and players described as the engine of the team.

The Dream go as she goes, and she went hard this series. Reese averaged 20.7 points and 7.6 rebounds over the three semifinal games. Her outsized presence in the paint, alongside the league's three leaders in steals, shut down the Liberty's ball movement and offensive threats. They barely led in the series, and couldn't hold onto a five-point lead at the beginning of the fourth. The Dream held New York scoreless from 9:26 of the fourth to 2:55, by which time Atlanta held an 81-75 lead.

The matchup between Reese and Liberty center Jonquel Jones lived up to the billing as most imperative to the series. Jones' own engine was in full gear for Game 3 with an early block of Reese, an offensive rebound and putback, and forcing Reese off course. Jones finished with 26 points (11 of 17) and 14 rebounds, countering Reese's 22 and 9. She was 7 of 18, her least efficient game of the series.

Reese is a master at, and makes no quiet deal of, getting under one's skin. It bubbled over in Game 3. In the second quarter, she dashed over to Sabrina Ionescu after the guard was called for an offensive foul on the screen and jawed at her all the way down the sideline. The teams converged; on her way back to the bench, Reese riled up the crowd.

Later in the frame, Jones denied Reese at the basket again, and they went face-to-face. A double technical was assessed for taunting.

Reese wasn't even on a legitimate contender when she clicked "post" on her social-media manifestation. The Sky, the team that drafted her No. 7 overall in 2024, finished tied for the worst record in the league. She had yet to reach the playoffs, despite 75% of the league making it in her rookie year when there were 12 teams.

She sent it after her season ended early and amid controversy when she said in an interview that for the Sky's front office, it was a "non-negotiable" that they needed to bring in "great players."

"So it's going to be very, very important this offseason to make sure we attract the best of the best because we can't settle for what we have this year," Reese told the Chicago Tribune .

When they could make a move after the collective bargaining agreement was approved, the Sky sent her to Atlanta. Her statements last fall weren't exactly manifestations. But they came true. She joined a stacked roster of all-WNBA talent fresh off a first-round exit in the playoffs.

"This is really going to make goals easier to attain," Reese said.

Smesko, the collegiate coach known for listing all of his players as "shooters," helped develop her game further than the rebounding for which she was best known. At one practice, he stopped drills until she made two 3s in a row in front of everyone.

It took patience then, and again throughout the season. The coaching staff encouraged her to shoot when it was available, knowing pre-All-Star they might not fall. But after All-Star, it would become natural.

She made 11 3s in the regular season, more than the seven combined she hit in her first two seasons in Chicago. In the semifinals, she made one each in the first two games. In Game 3, she hit two. The Dream have never lost when she hits a 3-pointer.

"That hasn't been something I've been able to show a lot, but now me being able to be confident in it, I think is probably my biggest thing coming to Atlanta," Reese said.

Her confidence in general, she said, "just continues to go through the roof." She credits the teammates and trust, in addition to adversity in Chicago and what was then described as a drop to No. 7 in the draft. She took advantage of her destiny, she said before Game 3.

Here she is after it, taking a victory lap of Barclays and snapping photos with fans and Dream personnel, headed to her first Finals.

"I'm just so thankful and I'm blessed to be able to be in this situation," Reese said. "A lot of people wish they were here, and I'm not gonna take this moment for granted. I'm here for a reason. We're all here for a reason."
